transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-12
Start: 16:00 PDT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Mark Rivera (ACME CTO), Jenna Park (Head of Search), Luis Gomez (ML Eng)

Auto-generated Summary (auto): quick hosted API walkthru focusing on embeddings endpoint and rerank endpoint, discussed vector DB choices, latency vs cost tradeoffs, security questions (SOC 2 / KMS / VPC options), next steps to run 1k-doc benchmark and share pricing

[00:00] Alex: hey everyone thanks for hopping on. i'm alex from redwood, this is priya our solutions engineer. today we're gonna run through the hosted api for embeddings and our rerank endpoint and show how you'd wire it into acme's search stack. any time you want to interrupt please do.

[00:18] Mark: yep thanks alex, quick context — we're reworking our relevance pipeline, current infra is elastic + custom bm25 + a light transformer reranker, latency targets are 150ms p99 for the user path. cost is also a big constraint.

[00:32] Priya: perfect, that's helpful. just to confirm, do you have a vector DB in prod? or are you looking to host vectors separately?

[00:40] Jenna: we currently use a hosted managed vector service for experiments but primary index is elastic. evaluating moving some traffic to vector re-rank flows.

[00:50] Priya: great, i'll demo two patterns: 1) use Redwood hosted embeddings for vector indexing (you push embeddings to your vector store like pinecone/milvus/FAISS) and call our rerank endpoint at query time for final scoring, and 2) an alternate where you use rerank-only with dense features if you generate embeddings in-house. i'll show latency and cost tradeoffs.

[01:12] Alex: quick note on security — hosted api supports SSO/SAML for console, we provide audit logs, and for enterprise we have dedicated and private options with VPC peering and KMS integrations.

[01:30] Jenna: can you say more about data residency and retention? we have customers in eu so that matters.

[01:36] Priya: yes — Hosted can pin region (we have eu-west region) and retention defaults can be configured; for stricter requirements we recommend Redwood Dedicated or Private where you control retention and key materials. we'll share the SOC 2 and security pack after.

[01:58] Alex: ok demo time — priya i'll hand it over.

[02:05] Priya: (screen) starting with the embeddings endpoint — it's a simple POST /v1/embeddings with model param, you can batch up to 512 docs per request depending on model and sequence length. here's an example payload and the shape of the vector returned. note that we support multiple open models and quantized variants; typical dims are 1536 and 768 depending on model.

[02:40] Jenna: what's your recommended dimension for rerank flow?

[02:44] Priya: for most semantic search rerank, 1536 gives better recall; 768 is cheaper and often close. if you're cost sensitive start with 768 and run a small eval. our Optimize product can recommend model+dim combos based on your eval sets.

[03:05] Luis: curious about throughput — we expect bursts during promo events. can hosted scale?

[03:12] Alex: yes Hosted supports autoscaling and burst capability; Dedicated provides more predictable tail latency for high QPS with reserved capacity. you can set routing policy to fall back to cheaper variant if capacity constrained.

[03:28] Priya: now the rerank endpoint — you submit candidate docs plus query embedding (or the raw query) and we return reranked scores and optional explanations. sample latency for our verified model on our hosted fleet is ~18-35ms per 10-candidate batch at p50; p95 varies by model and sequence length.

[03:52] Mark: that sounds promising but our p99 needs to be under 150ms end-to-end, including vector lookup time. how do folks typically architect that?

[04:05] Priya: common design: 1) fast ANN store (faiss/hnsw in milvus/pinecone) for candidate recall in ~10-30ms, 2) small candidate set (10-50) passed to Redwood rerank which adds ~20-80ms depending on model, so end-to-end can be under your 150ms if you tune candidate size and use batching/kv caching.

[04:30] Jenna: what's kv cache? we've seen it in docs but not sure how it helps.

[04:33] Priya: KV cache caches transformer key/value states for conversational or repeated queries to save compute. for single-shot rerank it helps if candidates share prefixes or if you do multi-turn. also automatic prefix caching can reduce per-token cost for generation use cases.

[04:50] Luis: any guidance on candidate set size for balancing recall vs latency?

[04:55] Priya: start with 10-20 candidates, run offline eval against your metrics. Redwood Optimize can suggest candidate sizes and model quantization profiles per workload.

[05:10] (short demo of api call flows, Priya pastes curl examples)

[05:28] Priya: here's a code snippet: call embeddings endpoint for your corpus -> index vectors in your store -> at query time call embeddings for the query -> ANN lookup -> call rerank with top-k candidates. we also support passing metadata and returning structured output for downstream scoring.

[05:45] Mark: how do you charge on the hosted side? embeddings tokens vs rerank token/time?

[05:50] Alex: pricing is usage-based: per-embedding unit (per vector) and per-rerank call which is roughly per token or per inference unit depending on model. for high volume we can do committed Dedicated pricing which lowers unit costs. i'll send the exact sheet.

[06:10] Jenna: any benchmarking you can share? i saw a brief doc but would prefer numbers on a 1k-doc sharded test with our typical queries.

[06:18] Priya: we can run a 1k-doc pilot using your anonymized dataset. we'll return latency distribution, token counts, and cost estimate. that's the plan for the action item.

[06:32] Luis: about vector db compatibility — we want to use milvus or self-hosted faiss. any gotchas?

[06:38] Priya: no hard dependency — any store that supports dense vectors works. we often see teams use milvus or pinecone. watch float precision and index type (HNSW params) — we'll share best-practice notes.

[06:55] Alex: competitors question — Mark, are you evaluating others like openai or their embeddings offering?

[07:02] Mark: yes, we have a PoC with OpenAI embeddings and a mid-size test on Pinecone. cost and tail latency are the main concerns. also need SOC2 and KMS.

[07:12] Priya: understood — we'll include SOC2 report, KMS integration docs, and an SSO onboarding note. for stricter compliance you can also deploy Redwood Private and run the control plane in your VPC.

[07:26] (Priya toggles to Console)

[07:30] Priya: quick look at Console — per-route dashboards show token breakdown, latency traces, and per-request logs. you can set rollout policies for models (canary, A/B) and tie regressions back to prompt sets. this is handy when you're tuning rerank thresholds.

[07:50] Jenna: do you capture user-level logs? we need audit trails for legal.

[07:54] Alex: yes audit logs and exportable traces; retention depends on plan. also for enterprise we can provide longer retention via add-on.

[08:06] Mark: curious about client-side integration: can we batch embedding uploads? we have a nightly reindex job.

[08:12] Priya: yes you can batch. we recommend chunking and using streaming upload for large corpora; chunk size depends on sequence length. for cost savings we suggest quantized models for indexing and full models for rerank.

[08:30] Luis: any tips on model selection/quantization?

[08:33] Priya: Optimize product recommends quant profiles by workload. in practice, we often use 8-bit quant for indexing vectors and a higher fidelity for rerank. we'll include suggested quant config in the benchmark report.

[08:48] (customer asks some follow-ups, short back-and-forth)

[09:05] Priya: last demo piece — streaming rerank isn't typical, but we do support low-latency calls and can integrate with your existing API gateway for fan-out. also you can do hybrid rerank where a fast sparse model filters and Redwood rerank refines top results.

[09:28] Mark: if we go forward with a pilot, what's an expected timeline to get meaningful results?

[09:34] Alex: typically 1-2 weeks: you provide an anonymized 1k dataset, we run bench and return results + recommended knobs. then a second week for integration.

[09:45] Jenna: what about cost estimate for POC? just rough.

[09:48] Priya: small pilot is usually under a few hundred dollars on Hosted; Dedicated requires contract but offers significant unit cost reductions for production. exact numbers in the pricing sheet.

[10:02] (questions about SLA and uptime)

[10:10] Alex: Hosted has published SLA for latency and uptime at the plan level; Dedicated/Private have contract SLAs. we'll include SLA language.

[10:20] (wrap up)

[10:24] Alex: ok let's recap — actions: priya runs bench and shares spreadsheet, alex sends pricing and security docs, acme to share dataset and confirm reviewers. schedule poc scoping next week. thanks all.

[10:40] Mark: thanks alex/priya, that was helpful, looking forward to the bench results.

[10:46] (call ends)

Notes: transcript has occasional transcription errors in names (console shows 'Redwoood' sometimes), timestamps approximate. references to shared artifacts: "1k-benchmark-template.xlsx" (to be shared), "security-pack.pdf" (to be shared).
